Earlier reports suggested that Apple is preparing to launch a 20th anniversary edition iPhone next year, featuring an all-glass design. However, analysts at investment bank Jefferies believe that the device is no longer moving forward.

Wall Street analysts say that the ambitious redesign plans for the 20th anniversary iPhone have been cancelled.

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform" today, with analyst Edison Lee noting that the possible cancellation of the 20th anniversary iPhone redesign is one of the main reasons for the downgrade.

The key to this downgrade lies in reports that Apple's all-glass iPhone project has been cancelled. Although rumours about the project being in development surfaced as early as 2025, with some expecting the product to launch in 2027, Apple has never responded to such speculation. However, Apple quietly filed a patent for an "all-glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies previously considered the launch of an all-glass iPhone to be reasonable and credible, but Edison Lee believes that development work has stalled. The analyst pointed out that supply chain checks indicate the project was terminated due to poor yield rates. Edison Lee believes that, with memory costs soaring, this decision is a "major blow" to driving high-end iPhone sales. He estimated that, had the device launched on schedule in September 2027 to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, its blended retail price would have reached US$2,060, higher than the average selling price of any previous model. Edison Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe Apple originally planned to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, thereby further increasing the average selling price and margins." He believes that, with memory prices rising, this move should have been an important defensive strategy.

Edison Lee also pointed out that Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are additional reasons contributing to the stock rating downgrade.

Based on Edison Lee's report, it is not entirely clear whether the analyst believes the entire redesign plan has been completely shelved, or whether only certain design elements have been abandoned.

The most upvoted comment was posted by Currentinterest.

These analysts have been wrong about Apple's future plans far too many times. Even the term "all-glass" has never accurately reflected Apple's true intentions. The 20th anniversary edition phone will be unique and innovative, and regardless of the final design, it will sell like hotcakes.

For example, there have long been rumours that Apple will not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an all-glass screen would be impossible. However, the rumoured quad-curved edge design may still be possible.

In any case, if the iPhone 20th anniversary edition design has indeed been cancelled, credible media outlets should soon confirm it.

What are your thoughts on this report regarding the iPhone 20th anniversary edition design? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
